E1.evidence: Public issue with a reproducer gist and observed output: "This example program outputs params {foo, ns1.bar, ns2.bar} as {p1, default_bar1, p3} respectively." Maintainer jacobperron: "I'm guessing it is simply a bug and not intended logic." Fixed by merged PR ros2/rclpy#1132 (merge commit 309f755d29fc734e457a03cb8e3f61da6d602a34).

E2.evidence:
The defect is an ordering error inside rclpy's own declare_parameters: the override lookup uses the not-yet-prefixed name. Reporter: "it attempts to load the user-supplied value from node._parameter_overrides[name] but at this point the namespace hasn't been prefixed to the name. This prefixing occurs on the code immediately following" (https://github.com/ros2/rclpy/issues/894#issuecomment-1035776371). Code at a5236920: "if not ignore_override and name in self._parameter_overrides:
    value = self._parameter_overrides[name].value

if namespace:
    name = f'{namespace}.{name}'". Both the parameter source (YAML / -p, parsed by rcl into _parameter_overrides) and the user code use the same fully qualified name convention (ns1.bar); the mismatch is between two statements of rclpy's own implementation, so it occurs with any correct caller and any correct parameter file. The fix (PR #1132) moves the prefixing above the lookup inside rclpy/rclpy/node.py only; no interface declaration changes.

E3.evidence: Would be PAIR (user code calls declare_parameters with namespace= and the parameter overrides from YAML/CLI are expected to flow in). Not decisive because the case stops at E2.

E4.evidence: Observed wrong value: "Parameters using the namespace argument of declare_parameters() cannot be loaded from sysargs (using -p) or from yaml config files."

notes: Ineligible internal: the wrong key is produced and consumed within rclpy's declare_parameters (override lookup before namespace prefixing). The fork commits under AIT-Assistive-Autonomous-Systems/rclpy are the PR #1132 branch commits; the ros2_test_prover commits are reproducer tests. Reported on Galactic (ros-galactic-rclpy 1.9.0); fix merged to rolling 2023-06-15.
